set.fa: Dallas Kloke and Bryce Simon, July 12, 1976. First winter ascent (to the summit ridge): Stuart Taylor and Ade Miller, March 13, 2005

findings.claim: FA date: stored 'July 1974 or 1976 (the year is recorded both ways)'; a peak page says 1972; the 1988 AAJ mentions 'the 1974 Kloke-Simon route'
findings.evidence: Primary account found: Bryce Simon's own note in the 1977 AAJ (1976 season): 'On July 12, Dallas Kloke and I climbed this 2000-foot face ... NCCS III, F6.' The 1977 Mountaineer annual has a report headed 'Davis Peak, North Face Couloir' giving 'July 12, 1976 by Bryce Simons and Dallas Kloke'. Beckey's Cascade Alpine Guide (1987 and 2008 editions, Google Books snippets) gives 'Kloke and Bryce Simon on July 12, 1976'. The 1981 Mountaineer annual also says Kloke and Simon climbed the NE face of Davis Peak in 1976. Three independent sources (AAJ primary account, Mountaineer annual, Beckey) agree on July 12, 1976. The 1972 figure (peak page) and the 1974 figure (a passing mention in a 1988 report on a different line) are secondary and unsupported. Removed the 'or 1974' clause and made the date exact.
sources: https://www.google.com/books/feeds/volumes?q=%22Davis+Peak%22+%22July+12,+1976%22 (The Mountaineer 1977; Cascade Alpine Guide 1987; Rainy Pass to Fraser River 2008)

findings.claim: first winter ascent date: stored March 13, 2005; TR title says 3/12/2005; Beckey 2008 says March 11, 2005
findings.evidence: The climbers' own trip report (posted Monday March 14, 2005; header 'Date of Climb: 3/12/2005') narrates: Friday night sleeping at Diablo; the next morning (Saturday March 12) the approach and a bivy at the glacier toe; 'the following morning' (Sunday March 13) the climb of the couloir and the descent. The 3/12 header is the trip start date. The AAJ 2005 summary gives March 13, 2005. Two independent sources agree on March 13 for the ascent. Beckey's 2008 guide says March 11, which nothing else supports. No change to that clause.

findings.claim: fa has no year; one route page says 1965, a magazine feature 1964
findings.evidence: Classic Cascade Climbs (Nelson, Whitelaw, Sjolseth, 2021; Google Books snippet): 'a route climbed in 1964 by Dan Davis and John Holland'. Climbing magazine's route feature also gives 1964. The route-database page for this route hosts a photo of Dan Davis's first-hand account of 'Index's first recorded route, June 21, 1964' (held at the UW Library). Only one route page gives 1965. Three sources give 1964 and one gives 1965, so the year is added. The June 21 day rests on the single photo caption and is not added. The FFA (1971) is not added either: it would be new material, not a correction.

wa_goode_mountain_megalodon_ridge.skip_reason: report only — pitch count is a classification column; owner decides

findings.claim: stored pitches 8; FA party belayed 7-8 and simul-climbed; one database says 20
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED that 8 is the FA party's belayed count, not the route's pitched-out count (report only)
findings.evidence: Pitched-out count: the route database gives '20 pitches, Grade IV', ~3,000 ft. The climbing-news account of the FA says the ridge would total more than 20 pitches if pitched out, and that 7-8 were belayed. These are the only two sources that state a pitched-out count, and the second comes from the FA party. The FA reports (AAJ, Alpinist) give no total, only: running belays along the crest, two 5.10 crack pitches, a down-led 5.10 pitch into Black Tooth Notch, and 'a few more pitches' to the summit. The only documented repeat (9/3/2010, a one-day push) was mostly unroped or simul-climbed. It pitched out 'a few pitches' on the snowy crest, bypassed the FA's crux pitches on mid-5th rock to the left, and roped up again from a couple hundred feet before Black Tooth Notch. It gives no count. The route database notes that rack size depends on how much a party simuls versus pitches out. So ~20 is the pitched-out figure (two sources), 7-8 belayed is what the FA party did, and the repeat belayed fewer. The stored overview already states both figures correctly.

pitches.evidence: Two sources give a pitched-out count of 20 / 20+. 8 is the FA party's belayed count while simul-climbing. Owner decides whether `pitches` means pitched-out length (20) or typical belayed leads (7-8).

wa_little_sister.skip_reason: report only — area elevation is not in the batch

findings.evidence: Map-based figures: one peak database gives 6,600+ ft (USGS 40-ft closed contour 6,600-6,640; 48.6924, -121.9764). A second peak list gives 6,620 ft (contour midpoint; same coordinate; Twin Sisters Mountain quad). The range page and a 2007 AAJ report give 6,600 ft. USGS 1 m lidar (EPQS), sampled on a fine grid around that coordinate, peaks at about 6,531 ft at 48.69232, -121.97651. One search index lists 6,535.8 ft (1,992.1 m), which matches the lidar. Lidar can clip a sharp rock summit, so ~6,530 is a lower bound. Every source falls between 6,530 and 6,640; none is near 6,017. Recommended single figure: 6,620 ft (contour midpoint, two agreeing lists), or 6,600 ft if the catalog prefers the lower contour. What 6,017 matches: not identified. A coarse lidar scan of a ~2 km box around the summit found no separate high point near 6,017 ft; ground at about 6,000 ft lies on the summit's own flanks ~300 m away (e.g. 5,957 ft at 48.6900, -121.9764). One possibility, not verified: the value is a ground sample at an offset area coordinate. Compare the stored area coordinate with 48.6924, -121.9764 before fixing.

area_elevation_ft.evidence: Contour 6,600-6,640 (two peak lists: 6,600+ and 6,620). Lidar ~6,531 is a lower bound. No source gives 6,017.
